questions.explanation: Labor demand derives from the marginal revenue product of labor. Average cost or fixed costs do not determine hiring.

questions.stem: A note asks what marginal product of labor measures; which?

options.text: Extra output from one more worker

questions.explanation: Marginal product is the additional output from one more worker. Average product divides total output by workers.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Labor demand from marginal revenue product
questions.stem: A clinician asks why labor demand is called derived demand; explain.

answer.exemplar: Labor demand is derived because firms demand workers only for the revenue those workers generate in producing goods and services; if product demand falls, labor demand falls too.

questions.explanation: Firms hire labor to produce output, so labor demand depends on product demand. It is not independent demand.

questions.stem: A clinician asks why compensating differentials persist in equilibrium; explain.

answer.exemplar: Compensating differentials persist because workers must be paid more to accept worse job attributes, and in equilibrium the higher pay just offsets the disamenity, leaving utility equal across jobs.

questions.explanation: Differentials equalize utility across jobs in equilibrium. Without them, workers would avoid bad jobs.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A clinician asks why MRP equals MPL times price under perfect competition; explain.

answer.exemplar: Under perfect competition the firm is a price taker, so marginal revenue equals price; thus MRP equals MPL times price, and the firm hires until that equals the wage.

questions.explanation: Perfect competition makes marginal revenue equal price, simplifying MRP. Monopolists use marginal revenue below price.
questions.hint: Price equals marginal revenue in competition.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Labor demand from marginal revenue product
questions.stem: A clinician asks why the labor demand curve slopes downward; reason through MRP and diminishing MPL.

answer.exemplar: As more workers are hired, diminishing marginal product lowers MPL, and with product price fixed, MRP falls; a lower wage is needed to justify hiring more, so labor demand slopes downward.

questions.explanation: Diminishing MPL reduces MRP, so firms hire more only at lower wages. Rising MPL would slope demand upward, which is wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A note asks why adding nurses to fixed equipment lowers marginal product; explain.

answer.exemplar: With fixed equipment, additional nurses share the same machines, causing congestion and lower individual contribution, so marginal product declines due to diminishing returns.

questions.explanation: Fixed capital creates diminishing returns as labor increases. Constant marginal product would require proportional capital.
